name: Baaseiah
overview: Baaseiah was a male Levite known specifically as the son of Malchijah, belonging to the Gershonite branch descended from Gershon, son of Levi. His identity is rooted in the priestly tribe of Levi, which held significant responsibilities in the worship and service of the LORD. As a Gershonite, Baaseiah was part of a distinct lineage within the Levites.
namesAndTitles: The name Baaseiah means "the LORD is bold," reflecting a declaration of God's strength and courage. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:40, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful theological affirmation consistent with the Levite heritage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Baaseiah as the son of Malchijah. Additionally, it is inferred that Michael was his father, situating Baaseiah within a specific family line among the Levites. Beyond this, no other familial relationships are detailed in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Baaseiah's significance lies in his place within the Levitical genealogies that established the organization and duties of the priestly tribe. As a Gershonite Levite, his lineage contributed to the preservation of the LORD's worship and the administration of sacred duties. His mention in 1 Chronicles 6:40 underscores the importance of genealogical records in maintaining the continuity of God's covenant people and their service in the tabernacle.
